evals.prompt: it's wednesday and i just had a 1:1 with Sarah. she mentioned that the team offsite needs a different venue because the original one fell through. also Alex from platform wants to set up a security review for their new service mesh changes. can you add these to my worklog?
evals.expected_output: Should add two items to the EXISTING week file without creating a new week or archiving. Should create a People stub for Alex if she doesn't exist. Should NOT trigger a rollover.
evals.issue_tested: Issue #2 and #3 - mid-week updates should not create new week files

evals.prompt: /worklog review
evals.expected_output: Should walk through items one by one and collect updates. Should NOT create a new week file or archive the current week unless it's actually Monday and a new week has started. The review command description currently conflates review with rollover.
evals.issue_tested: Issue #2 - review command creates new week every time

evals.prompt: /worklog audit
evals.expected_output: Stuck items check should work correctly. But since archived weeks only have summary bullets (no priority markers or item titles), the audit can only detect stuck items by comparing the current active week against rollover notes in archives. Should not crash or produce false positives from archived files.
evals.issue_tested: Issue #4 - stuck item detection across archive format

evals.prompt: /worklog add P1 quick sync with Marcus about the API rate limit proposal
evals.expected_output: Should add the item and wiki-link Marcus Williams. Should NOT do a full frontmatter regeneration just for adding one sub-item. Or if it does regen, it should be fast and not glob 60+ files for a minor edit.
evals.issue_tested: Issue #5 - frontmatter regen overhead on minor edits

evals.prompt: /worklog viz quarter
evals.expected_output: Should produce a self-contained HTML file with 4 D3 charts. The HTML should be consistent in structure across invocations - same chart types, same color scheme, same layout. Without a template, each invocation may produce wildly different HTML.
evals.issue_tested: Issue #7 - viz consistency without template

evals.prompt:
here are notes from my 1:1 with Sarah Chen:
- she's concerned about the migration timeline slipping
- wants to bring in a contractor for the gap
- mentioned that Marcus is doing well picking up Dev's work

add to worklog
evals.expected_output: Should process these as sub-items under the existing Sarah Chen / Dev leave item. Should NOT create a duplicate top-level item. Should add dated annotations with today's date.
evals.issue_tested: Issue #3 - transcript/notes processing flow

evals.prompt: /worklog summary month
evals.expected_output: If run twice in the same month, the second run overwrites the first without warning. Should either warn or append a date suffix to avoid silent data loss.
evals.issue_tested: Issue #8 - summary overwrite without warning

evals.prompt: /worklog pull
evals.expected_output: On first run with empty Sources/ directory: should walk the user through registering one channel - ask for channel name, resolve via slack_search_channels, write Sources/<channel-name>.md with type=meeting-notes-via-email, channel_id, last_scan_ts=null, nudge_threshold_days=5, first_scan_lookback_days=14. Then proceed with the first pull.
evals.issue_tested: First-run registration flow when no Sources/ files exist

evals.prompt: /worklog pull (run a second time within seconds, no new Slack content)
evals.expected_output: Should be idempotent: no new Meetings/ files created, no existing files modified, no items added to current week file. Should advance Sources/<channel>.md last_scan_ts to current time. Summary should report 0 new threads, 0 updated, 0 items extracted.
evals.issue_tested: Idempotency - re-running pull with no new Slack content must not duplicate or rewrite anything

evals.prompt: /worklog pull (with 1 existing Meetings/ note that has new replies in Slack since last_scan_ts)
evals.expected_output: Should look up slack_thread_ts in existing Meetings/*.md frontmatter, find the match, fetch only replies after slack_last_reply_ts, append them to ## Discussion with chronological date/author subheadings in user's local timezone, update slack_last_reply_ts in frontmatter, and run extraction on the appended content only. Should NOT rewrite ## Notes or any other existing content. Should NOT create a new Meetings note for the same thread_ts.
evals.issue_tested: Thread evolution - existing threads with new replies append cleanly without overwriting

evals.prompt: /worklog rollover (with Sources/<channel>.md last_scan_ts older than 5 days)
evals.expected_output: Should prepend a one-line FYI before continuing with rollover: 'FYI - last pulled #channel-name N days ago. Run /worklog pull to ingest. Continuing with rollover...' Then perform the normal rollover. Should NOT block, hijack the command, or auto-pull.
evals.issue_tested: Stale-channel nudge surfaces on rollover when threshold exceeded

evals.prompt: /worklog add P1 sync with Sarah about hiring (with Sources/<channel>.md last_scan_ts older than 5 days)
evals.expected_output: Should add the item normally without surfacing the stale-channel nudge. /worklog add is not in the nudge-eligible command set; only rollover, tidy, and audit are.
evals.issue_tested: Stale-channel nudge does NOT surface on commands outside the nudge-eligible set

evals.prompt: /worklog pull (with 1 new thread; auto-fetch helper at ~/.config/obsidian-worklog/bin/slack-fetch-file is configured and a valid files:read token is at ~/.config/obsidian-worklog/slack-token)
evals.expected_output: Should attempt auto-fetch FIRST: shell out to ~/.config/obsidian-worklog/bin/slack-fetch-file <file_id> with the top-of-thread file attachment ID. On success (helper exits 0, prints body to stdout): use that body as the source content, do NOT prompt the user. Convert HTML to plain markdown, strip email-client chrome, build the Meetings/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md note with frontmatter, run the existing Processing raw input pipeline to extract action items into the current week file, advance last_scan_ts past the thread. The full ingest is automatic with no user paste step.
evals.issue_tested: v5.4.0 auto-fetch happy path - helper script returns body, skill ingests without prompting

evals.prompt: /worklog pull (with 1 new thread; helper script not installed OR token file missing OR token expired/revoked)
evals.expected_output: Should attempt auto-fetch first; helper exits non-zero (or doesn't exist). Should fall back to manual-paste prompt: present thread summary including a one-line note about the auto-fetch error, ask user to paste body or say 'skip' / 'skip all remaining'. On paste: same downstream pipeline as auto-fetch path. Should NOT silently fail; should NOT skip the thread without user confirmation; should NOT block the entire pull (other threads are processed normally).
evals.issue_tested: v5.4.0 auto-fetch fallback - manual paste path remains fully functional when helper is missing or fails

evals.prompt: /worklog pull (one meeting-notes-via-email source and one context-channel source registered)
evals.expected_output: Should branch on type: run the existing per-thread Meetings flow for the email source, and the sweep-and-classify flow for the context-channel source. The two must not interfere. Context-channel must NOT create Meetings/ notes. Email source behavior is unchanged.
evals.issue_tested: Source-type branch - both pull modes coexist in one /worklog pull

evals.prompt: /worklog pull (context-channel with a thread that clearly names a program already tracked as a worklog item)
evals.expected_output: Should classify the thread as a high-confidence match and auto-fold it as a dated sub-item under the matching worklog item, wiki-linked, with a Slack permalink for provenance and the Slack timestamp as the date. Should NOT prompt for this item. Should list the auto-fold in the end-of-pull summary (summary -> target item + permalink).
evals.issue_tested: High-confidence match auto-folds with provenance and is itemized in the summary

evals.prompt: /worklog pull (context-channel with one weakly-related thread and one clearly-new decision thread)
evals.expected_output: Should stage BOTH into a single end-of-pull approval batch (a numbered chat checklist) - the weak one as an uncertain match proposing attachment to a candidate item, the new one as a proposed new item with priority and subgroup. Nothing is written until the user responds. Should never force-fit the weak match. A bulk reply (e.g. 'add 1; 2 as P2 under X; skip') applies edits correctly and regenerates frontmatter only if a top-level item was added.
evals.issue_tested: Weak + new candidates batch for approval; no force-fit; bulk edit applies

evals.prompt: /worklog pull (context-channel containing only unrelated banter and logistics)
evals.expected_output: Should classify all units as noise and drop them silently - zero writes to any worklog item or note, no approval-batch entries. The summary reports them as dropped (count only).
evals.issue_tested: Noise is dropped silently with no writes

evals.prompt: /worklog pull (run a second time within seconds against the same context-channel, no new Slack content)
evals.expected_output: Should be idempotent: ts > last_scan_ts yields no new units, so no auto-folds, no approval batch, no writes. last_scan_ts advances to current time. Summary reports 0 scanned/0 folded/0 surfaced/0 dropped for that channel.
evals.issue_tested: Context-channel idempotency via last_scan_ts

evals.prompt: /worklog pull (context-channel whose window contains more than ~100 conversation units)
evals.expected_output: Should hit the volume guardrail: stop and tell the user the unit count and the window, and ask whether to proceed, narrow the window, or skip the channel. Should NOT silently truncate or silently analyze only a subset.
evals.issue_tested: Volume guardrail - no silent truncation on large windows

evals.prompt: /worklog pull (Sources/_dms.md enabled, slack-search-dms helper present and scope/consent granted, plus context-channel sources)
evals.expected_output: Should process channel sources, then run the DM sweep after them: call slack-search-dms with after=last_scan_ts and channel_types from include_1on1/include_groups, paginate via next_cursor, classify each result against the vault. DM candidates join the SAME end-of-pull approval batch as context-channel uncertain/new items. NOTHING from a DM is auto-folded.
evals.issue_tested: DM-sweep branch runs after channels via search; DM items batch, never auto-fold

evals.prompt: /worklog pull (a DM search result clearly matches a tracked worklog item)
evals.expected_output: Should present the DM match in the approval batch with a recommended 'attach as sub-item under [[item]]' option - NOT write it silently. Unlike a context-channel high-confidence match, a DM high-confidence match is never auto-folded.
evals.issue_tested: DM high-confidence match goes to approval batch, not auto-fold

evals.prompt: /worklog pull then approve a DM-derived item from the batch
evals.expected_output: On approval, the folded sub-item is a genericized, workstream-level summary (no verbatim 1:1 quote, no personal detail beyond the item's need), dated with the result's message_ts, wiki-linked, with the result's permalink for provenance.
evals.issue_tested: Approved DM items fold as genericized summaries with provenance

evals.prompt: /worklog pull (Sources/_dms.md enabled but slack-search-dms missing, scope absent, or consent not granted so the helper returns non-zero)
evals.expected_output: Should run the helper, get a non-zero exit (e.g. missing_scope), print a one-line 'DM sweep skipped: <reason>' note, and continue/complete the rest of the pull normally. Must NOT block or fail the whole pull.
evals.issue_tested: Helper missing/unauthorized/not-consented -> DM sweep skipped gracefully

evals.prompt: /worklog pull (_dms.md has exclude_users and exclude_conversations populated)
evals.expected_output: Search results whose channel_id is in exclude_conversations, and whose author_user_id is in exclude_users, are dropped before classification - their content never enters the approval batch. include_1on1/include_groups are honored by selecting channel_types.
evals.issue_tested: DM exclusions filter search results before classification

evals.prompt: /worklog pull (run twice with no new DM activity)
evals.expected_output: Second run: search with after=last_scan_ts returns no results, no batch entries, no writes; last_scan_ts advances to now. Idempotent.
evals.issue_tested: DM-sweep idempotency via global last_scan_ts as the search after filter

evals.prompt: /worklog pull (DM search yields more than max_results results, next_cursor still set at the cap)
evals.expected_output: Should hit the volume guardrail up front: stop and tell the user the count and window, ask whether to proceed / narrow / skip. No silent truncation.
evals.issue_tested: DM-sweep volume guardrail at max_results - no silent truncation

evals.prompt: i'm adding a worklog note: 'Met with Brian and Astha about the Cloud Security migration; Chris is reviewing.' Wrap the people and programs as wiki-links.
evals.expected_output: Should run cross-link-index.sh (NOT glob People/Programs, NOT read bodies) to get the entity/alias digest. Should link [[Brian Gaines|Brian]] (the dominant referent), [[Astha Singhal|Astha]], and [[Cloud Security]]. For the ambiguous 'Chris' (multiple people, no dominant referent), should ask which Chris or leave it unlinked rather than guessing.
evals.issue_tested: cross-link-index helper: writes consult the digest instead of globbing; dominant alias auto-links, ambiguous alias is not guessed (Brian-dominant is vault-data-driven; confirmed prod vault 2026-06)

evals.prompt: /worklog viz quarter
evals.expected_output: Model Guard behavior: if running on a sub-Opus model (Sonnet/Haiku), should pause and ask whether to continue or switch to Opus 4.8 before generating the visualization, and ask at most once per conversation. If running on Opus-tier or if the model cannot determine its identity, should proceed silently with no guard prompt. Light commands (add/review/audit) must never trigger the guard.
evals.issue_tested: Model Guard fires on heavy commands under sub-Opus, fails open otherwise
